MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "The Essential Kinks feels like a natural next choice after the Beatles and mid-'60s hits because it connects familiar classic rock with the retrospective collections I often choose.",
    "Carly Simon fits the melodic singer-songwriter appeal of Simon & Garfunkel and Melanie, while That's Christmas To Me follows my recent interest in A Very Special Christmas."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "Willie Nelson and John Michael Montgomery offer collections of hits, but that format alone does not make country music what I want right now.",
    "Cheek to Cheek does not mean I would choose any jazz album, and my interest in holiday music does not imply an interest in a gospel collection.",
    "The Hit Singles Collection leaves me unsure whose songs I would hear, while Little Broken Hearts and Us And The Night give me less reason to expect the familiar songs I am seeking."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "Choosing greatest-hits albums seems to have been treated as interest in collections regardless of the artist or music.",
    "An occasional choice outside classic pop and rock seems to have been taken as a broader interest than my history supports."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "My repeated choices of classic rock, mid-'60s songs, and melodic singer-songwriters matter more than whether an album is a career collection.",
    "My latest Christmas album makes another holiday album timely, but that interest is specific to holiday listening.",
    "Recognizing the artist and expecting songs I enjoy matters when I decide whether to try a collection."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "You picked up on my interest in familiar collections and holiday music, but sometimes missed the specific artists and musical connections that make those choices appealing."
}
